    Popups

    Popups use a panel-local LIFO stack that is independent of the Navigation Graph. Each call clones a VisualTreeAsset, optionally assigns a data source, animates it into the panel, and returns an awaitable result.

    Set up a host

    Add UIPopupHost to the GameObject that owns the panel's PanelRenderer. The host requires that component and creates its popup layer when PanelRenderer supplies a UI root.

    public sealed class PopupExample : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private UIPopupHost popupHost;
    [SerializeField] private VisualTreeAsset messagePopup;
}

    Call Show only after the panel root has been initialized. Calling it before the UI root is ready throws an InvalidOperationException.

    Build a popup template

    Every popup VisualTreeAsset must contain:

    • exactly one UIPopupView;
    • exactly one UIPopupContent inside that View;
    • zero or one UIPopupBackdrop inside that View.

    Invalid counts throw an exception that includes the number found. The failed instance is rolled back and is not left on the stack.

    <ui:UXML xmlns:ui="UnityEngine.UIElements"
         xmlns:popup="NKStudio.UITKNavigation.Popup">
    <popup:UIPopupView close-on-backdrop="false" back-behavior="Close">
        <popup:UIPopupBackdrop />
        <popup:UIPopupContent>
            <ui:Label>
                <Bindings>
                    <ui:DataBinding property="text"
                                    data-source-path="Title"
                                    binding-mode="ToTarget" />
                </Bindings>
            </ui:Label>

            <ui:VisualElement name="dynamic-content" />

            <popup:UIPopupActionButton text="Cancel"
                action-id="cancel" close-popup="true" />
            <popup:UIPopupActionButton text="OK"
                action-id="confirm" close-popup="true" />
        </popup:UIPopupContent>
    </popup:UIPopupView>
</ui:UXML>

    The package supplies full-panel positioning and these USS classes: ui-popup-view, ui-popup-backdrop, ui-popup-content, and ui-popup-action-button. Your template USS is responsible for Backdrop color, Content placement and size, spacing, and typography.

    Show and await a popup

    Use ShowAsync when only the final result matters:

    UIPopupResult result = await popupHost.ShowAsync(
    messagePopup,
    new MessagePopupModel { Title = "Notice" },
    configure: view =>
        view.Q("dynamic-content")?.Add(new Label("Runtime content")),
    cancellationToken: cancellationToken);

Debug.Log($"Action={result.ActionId}, Reason={result.Reason}");

    Annotate model properties used by UI Toolkit data binding with [CreateProperty] from Unity.Properties. The model becomes the UIPopupView.dataSource before Show.

    Use Show when you also need the handle:

    UIPopupHandle handle = popupHost.Show(messagePopup, model);

handle.ActionInvoked += actionId =>
    Debug.Log($"Invoked: {actionId}");

UIPopupResult result = await handle.Completion;

    UIPopupHandle.IsOpen remains true until the Hide transition finishes. Call handle.Close() for that specific instance, popupHost.CloseTop() for the top item, or popupHost.CloseAll() for the entire host.

    Actions and results

    UIPopupActionButton trims and raises its action-id. With close-popup="true", it closes the popup and returns that ID. With false, it raises ActionInvoked but leaves Completion pending until something else closes the popup.

    Close reason Produced by
    Action An action button that closes the popup
    Back Back behavior Close
    Backdrop A direct Backdrop click with close-on-backdrop="true"
    Programmatic Close, CloseTop, or CloseAll
    HostDetached Host disable, panel root reload, or detach

    Cancellation is different from a close result. A canceled token removes the instance immediately and completes the task as canceled. If the token is already canceled, the template is not instantiated.

    Stack, Back, and focus

    The last popup shown is the first one closed. Only the topmost, non-closing popup receives the high-priority Back policy:

    Back behavior Result
    Close Closes the top popup and consumes Back
    Block Keeps the popup open and consumes Back
    PassThrough Keeps it open and lets Back continue to the graph or a lower handler

    When shown, the popup focuses its first enabled focusable descendant. When the top popup closes, focus returns to the previously focused element; if that element no longer exists, focus moves to the popup below.

    close-on-backdrop reacts only when the Backdrop itself is the click target. Clicking a child placed inside the Backdrop does not count as a direct Backdrop click.

    Popup transitions

    UIPopupView provides separate Backdrop Transitions and Content Transitions, each with independent Show/Hide presets and channels. Both layers play together and the longer finite layer determines completion. Closing does not complete the handle until Hide finishes.

    Avoid infinite Hide loops, because the popup cannot finalize while its Hide transition never completes. See Transition animation for preset, timing, reversal, and Loop details.
